question:
A 34-year-old male presents to the clinic one day after sustaining an injury to his left ankle while
playing soccer. He reports tripping over another player’s foot, rolling his ankle inward, hearing a ‘pop,’
and experiencing sharp pain immediately afterward. He was able to bear some weight on the foot
shortly after the injury. Examination of the left lower extremity reveals that his foot prefers inversion,
with noticeable laxity at the ankle joint. Although he can bear weight, he describes moderate pain.
Which additional finding is most likely on physical examination? Answer Choices: (A) Ecchymosis over
medial aspect (B) Proximal fibular head posterior (C) Calcaneus deviated laterally (D) Decreased
range of plantar flexion (E) Positive Thompson test (F) Distal fibula posterior (G) Talar tilt toward
midline (H) Medial malleolus tender to palpation (I) Point tenderness over deltoid ligament (J) Left foot
in dorsiflexion
 A. Calcaneus deviated laterally
B. Proximal fibular head posterior
C. Medial malleolus tender to palpation
D. Distal fibula posterior
E. Left foot in dorsiflexion
F. Ecchymosis over medial aspect
G. Talar tilt toward midline
H. Positive Thompson test
I. Point tenderness over deltoid ligament
J. Decreased range of plantar flexion
